ellie: Quick check — running into intermittent 401s when using service account impersonation with the node streaming client. Works for short non-stream requests but streams often fail right at connect with `invalid_token` in the logs. Anyone seen this pattern?

ajay: Which token flow are you using? JWT->access_token exchange (oauth token) or OIDC target_audience (id_token)?

ellie: We're doing SA impersonation: calling STS to exchange a signed JWT for an access token, then passing that in Authorization: Bearer. Non-streaming calls are fine. Streaming connect sometimes returns `401: {"error":"invalid_token","error_description":"audience mismatch"}`.

ajay: That sounds like the stream endpoint expects an id_token (target_audience) for auth in some configurations. If you accidentally set the JWT aud to the wrong value the STS response can be a token that's rejected by the streaming front proxy.

ajay: quick diagnostic: print the access token JWT header/payload (or use jwt.io) and check the `aud` claim. It should match the STS/Audience we expect. Also check whether the streaming ingress is configured to accept access tokens vs id_tokens.

samir: fwiw the node client historically supports both but the streaming path has stricter checking on our side (we validate aud against a short list). If the exchanged token contains the service account email as aud instead of the expected gateway audience you'll get that error.

ellie: here's the minimal log and the exchange call we make:

```
POST https://sts.googleapis.com/v1/token
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer&assertion=<signed_jwt>

// response: access_token=ya29... expires_in=3600

// stream connect:
POST /v1/stream:connect
Authorization: Bearer ya29...
-> 401 {"error":"invalid_token","error_description":"audience mismatch"}
```

ellie: any recommended changes?

ajay: Two options:
1) Use an id_token via the STS target_audience flow (if your ingress accepts id_tokens). That means set `aud` of the signed JWT to the STS audience for target_audience and request `requested_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token`.
2) Update the gateway to accept the access token audience you're producing. Usually that's done only for internal lanes.

ajay: Example (node) to request id_token from STS:```js
const body = new URLSearchParams({
  grant_type: 'urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer',
  assertion: signedJwt,
  requested_token_type: 'urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token',
  audience: 'https://redwood.example.com' // gateway audience
});
const r = await fetch('https://sts.googleapis.com/v1/token', { method: 'POST', body });
const j = await r.json();
const idToken = j.id_token;
```

kevin: tagging my review hat — if we go with id_tokens we should add a small integration test to the runtime to ensure streaming accepts id_tokens from STS. I can pick that up if ellie opens a PR.

ellie: thanks — I can prototype a small change. Question on retries: if a stream fails during connect with a 401, does our node client attempt any retry/refresh automatically? I saw some reconnect logic but not sure it requests a fresh token.

samir: short answer: no, streaming connect failures are not retried by the SDK automatically (because refresh+retry can lead to duplicate connections and complex resume behavior). We do auto-refreshs for non-stream calls. For streams we expect the app/client to handle token refresh then reconnect.

samir: pattern we've recommended: wrap the stream connect in a 3-attempt backoff, but the reconnect flow should explicitly call your token refresh/impersonation routine before retrying connect. Example pseudo:```js
async function connectWithRetry() {
  for (let i=0;i<3;i++){
    const token = await getFreshImpersonatedToken();
    try { return await client.connect({ auth: token }); }
    catch (e){ if (is401(e) && i<2) await sleep(2**i * 250); else throw e; }
  }
}
```

ellie: OK makes sense. I'll change our helper to request id_token instead and add the retry wrapper.

ajay: also check service account impersonation TTLs — if you're minting short-lived tokens client-side, ensure you don't accidentally reuse expired tokens between the exchange and the connect (race condition). Print token expiry and compare to now during debug.

kevin: sounds good. If you want I can also add a small comment in the runtime docs under "Auth for streaming" to highlight id_token vs access_token differences.

ellie: please do. I'll include a short paragraph and the code snippet. ETA for PR: EOD PST.

ajay: FYI I left a small note in the internal auth playbook: https://redwood.internal/docs/auth/sts-impersonation — put the id_token example under the streaming section.

ellie: awesome. One more logistics Q — can we tag this for tomorrows morning standup? I want a 2-min sync if integration test uncovers anything.

samir: sure, add it to the standup board or ping ops. I'll be there.

ellie: done. thanks everyone! :sparkles:
